description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Instrumental builds a manufacturing acceleration platform that uses production data and AI to help electronics manufacturers improve yield, throughput, and product ramp. The Backend Engineer builds and improves product backend services, owns features through the software development lifecycle, and supports production quality and reliability.
Backend Engineer owning the full software lifecycle for product services, building features and validating production reliability and performance

Responsibilities:
• Own the full software development lifecycle across design, implementation, testing, deployment, release and validation
• Build and improve the backend services behind our product, learning to balance shipping quickly with writing code that’s simple and easy to maintain
• Take responsibility for the quality of features in production by validating your work, investigating issues, and improving performance and reliability
• Use AI-assisted development tools to move faster and share what works with the team
• Spot technical debt and tooling gaps in your area and bring well-reasoned proposals for what to tackle
• Work with engineers across teams to deliver features that support our product, AI, and edge systems

Requirements:
• 1–2 years as a software engineer, ideally at a startup or on a small team where you shipped code that real users depended on
• You've owned a feature or component from start to finish, including scoping it, building it, getting it to production, and fixing it when it broke, even if someone more senior shaped the overall design
• Comfort working through problems that aren't fully defined. You ask good questions, make reasonable calls when you don't have every answer, and learn from how those calls turn out
• Solid working knowledge of Python or Go, plus a genuine interest in data modeling and system design and a desire to get much better at both
• You use AI-assisted development tools as part of your everyday workflow and are eager to share what's working with your teammates
• Signs that you grow quickly, such as taking on more responsibility over time, picking up feedback fast, or being the person teammates came to for a particular area
